fit: you are opening a new practice or location and need a professional website from day one
your current site looks dated, is hard to use on a phone or rarely produces a call
you serve patients in more than one language and want your site to speak to them in both
medical-website-design.plain: A medical website is your practice's front door online: the place where patients read about your treatments, decide whether they trust you, and call or request an appointment. Almost every patient looks a practice up before booking, and every ad, search result and social post you run sends people back to the site. We design and program each one from scratch so it loads quickly, reads clearly on a phone and makes contacting your office the obvious next step.

steps.d: We talk through your goals, budget, the treatments you want to grow and the sites you like or dislike. If you already have a website, we review it and tell you what is worth keeping.
Your assigned designer draws the layout of the home page and main pages so you can see the structure before anything is built. You tell us what to change and approve the direction.

Our designers and programmers build the full site and prepare the text, with AI helping on research and first drafts and our team reviewing every page. You provide photos, provider bios and logos, and a physician checks the medical content.

We test the site on phones, tablets and computers, check every form and phone number, then publish it once you sign off. After launch we show your staff how to make edits, and you watch the call reports to see what the site brings in.

tools.d: This is the private editing area behind your website, similar to working in a word processor. We set it up and train your staff so routine updates do not depend on us.
These are phone numbers that ring at your front desk as usual but record that the call came from your website. We use them to show you how many patient calls the site produces.

These are software tools that can research topics, draft text and help check pages for errors. We use them to speed up the early work, and our team reviews everything before it goes live, with physician review for medical content.

A blog is a section of your site for short articles, and integration means your site links to your social media profiles. We build both in so new articles and posts keep the site current and give patients more ways to reach you.

glossary.d: A way of building a website so its layout automatically adjusts to fit a phone, tablet or computer screen.
The moment a website visitor takes the action you want, such as calling your office or sending an appointment request.
The work of organizing and writing a website so search engines like Google understand it and show it to people searching for your services.

deliverables.d: A look created from a blank page around your specialty, your taste and your budget, not a template shared with other practices.
Every page is laid out for a small screen first and loads quickly, because most patients will visit from their phone.
Pages are organized and labeled so Google can read what you treat and where you are, which helps patients find you.
You get a simple login where your staff can change text, photos, hours and blog posts without calling a programmer.
Patients can request appointments or complete paperwork from home, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact.
You can see the phone calls your website produces, and you can reach our staff by phone when you need help.

fit: you are a physician adding aesthetic treatments and need a site that presents them as a real part of your practice
your current website looks dated or generic next to the experience patients get in your office
you want one team to handle the site, social media and email instead of coordinating several vendors
medical-spa-website-design.plain: A medical spa website is your practice's online front door: a custom-designed site that presents your treatments, your team and your setting the way patients experience them in person. Most patients look up a practice before they call, so the site has to look right and also be easy to find on search engines and in answers from AI assistants. Our in-house team designs and builds it, then pairs it with the social media and email marketing that bring patients to it.

steps.d: We ask about your practice, the treatments you want to grow and the patients you want to reach. You tell us your priorities and share any existing logo, colors, photos and website access.
We present a design for the site and draft the text for each page. You review both, correct anything that does not sound like your practice, and approve the treatment descriptions.

Our programmers build the approved design and connect booking, forms and your electronic medical record system where needed. Anything that touches patient data is set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact, so we need that person available.

We publish the site, then keep it maintained and adjust it as search engines and AI assistants change how they show results. You send us news, new treatments, staff changes and photos as they come up.

tools.d: The software behind a website that stores its pages, text and images and lets them be edited without rebuilding the site. We build your site on one so updates such as a new treatment or a new provider can be made quickly.

A scheduling tool that shows patients available times and takes their appointment requests through the website. We add it to your site and link it to the calendar or practice software your staff already uses, where that is possible.

Labels added to a page's code, invisible to visitors, that tell search engines exactly what the page contains, such as your address, hours and services. We add them so Google and AI assistants can describe your practice accurately.

Software that can draft and summarize text, and that now answers many patient questions directly in search results. We use it to assist with first drafts and research, and our writers and physician staff review everything before it goes live. It never gives medical advice to patients.

glossary.d: The work of organizing and writing a website so search engines understand it and show it to people looking for the services you offer.
A way of building a site so its layout adjusts automatically to fit a phone, tablet or desktop screen.
A button or short line of text that tells a visitor what to do next, such as booking a consultation.

deliverables.d: A site designed from scratch around your brand, photos and treatment menu, with no templates, so it looks like your practice.
Pages explaining each treatment in plain language, drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by our physician staff before they are published.
A booking tool on the site that lets patients request consultations and treatments at any hour, without calling your front desk.
A second language version of your pages, such as Spanish, so more patients in your area can read about your services.
Social media pages and email newsletters, written with our physician staff, that keep your practice in front of current and prospective patients.
Ongoing updates, fixes and content changes handled by our staff, with a phone number you can call to reach a person.

fit: you already pay for ads and the clicks currently go to your home page
you are promoting a specific treatment, seasonal offer or event and want it to have its own page
your web inquiries often sit unanswered until someone at the front desk has a free moment
landing-pages-funnels.plain: A landing page is a single web page built around one treatment, promotion or event, with one clear next step such as requesting a consultation. A patient funnel is the full path around that page: the ad that brings the patient in, the form they fill out and the follow-up messages that help them book. Practices need this because a patient who clicks an ad for one treatment and arrives on a general home page has to hunt for the answer, and many leave before they find it.

steps.d: We talk through the treatment, the kind of patient you want to reach and the single action the page should ask for. You provide the offer details, your credentials and any patient photos you have written consent to use.
AI tools help us draft the page and several variations, then our writers edit them and our physician advisors review the medical claims. You read the page and approve it before anything is published.

We link the form to the follow-up messages and to the way your office handles new inquiries, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact. You tell us who receives the inquiries and when they can respond.

Once the page is live, we run tests, read the results and adjust the page on a regular schedule. You let us know which inquiries turned into consultations so we improve the page based on real patients, not just form submissions.

tools.d: Software for creating standalone web pages that sit alongside your main website without rebuilding it. We use it to publish each campaign page and to change it quickly when a test shows a better version.

Software that can draft text from instructions. We use it to produce first drafts and alternate headlines faster, and every page is edited by our team and reviewed by a physician advisor before it goes live.
A system that sends pre-written messages the moment a form is submitted. We use it for confirmations and scheduling reminders only, and these messages never give medical advice.
Measurement tools that record how visitors arrive on a page and what they do there. We set them up so you can see which ad led to which inquiry, without relying on guesswork.

glossary.d: The moment a visitor takes the action the page asks for, such as submitting a consultation request.
The button or line of text that tells the patient what to do next, for example "Request a consultation".
A person who has shared their contact details and shown interest but has not yet booked an appointment.

deliverables.d: A dedicated page for each treatment, promotion or event, written to answer the patient's question and point to one action.
A clear offer and a short form that asks only for what your front desk needs to schedule a consultation.
Before-and-after galleries, frequently asked questions and physician credentials, arranged so patients can judge your practice before they contact you.
Automatic messages that confirm a patient's request right away and tell them what happens next, so inquiries do not go cold.
Side-by-side trials of headlines, offers and layouts, with a plain summary of which version brought in more consultation requests.
A report that follows each inquiry from the ad click to the booked consultation, showing which campaigns fill your schedule.

fit: you already recommend or sell products in the office and patients ask how to get more between visits
your front desk spends time taking reorders by phone and you would like those orders to come in online
you want to sell products under your practice's name but do not have staff who can build or run an online store
medical-e-commerce.plain: An online medical store is a section of your practice website where patients can browse the skincare, supplements and other products you recommend, pay by card and have them shipped or set aside for pickup. It lets patients reorder between visits without calling the front desk, and it keeps those purchases with your practice instead of a general retailer. Our programmers build the store, connect the payments and load your products, so your staff does not have to learn e-commerce to get started.

steps.d: We talk through what you want to sell, how you want to be paid and how orders will reach patients. You provide your product list, prices and any rules your suppliers set for selling online.
We design the store, build the cart and open or connect your merchant account. You supply business and bank details for the payment application and decide on shipping, pickup and return policies.

We add your products, then place test orders to confirm that payments, taxes, shipping charges and confirmation emails all work. You review every product page and the checkout before anything goes public.
We open the store to patients and show your staff how to see and fill orders. After that we host and maintain it, and you tell us when products, prices or stock change.

tools.d: This is the software that runs the store: it displays products, manages the cart and records each order. We install it on your practice website and configure it so your staff can look up orders in one place.

A payment gateway is the service that takes the card details a patient types in and passes them safely to the bank for approval. We connect it to your checkout so card numbers are handled by the payment processor and are not stored on your website.

Digital wallets such as Apple Pay and Google Pay let a patient pay with a card already saved on their phone or computer. We add them at checkout so patients on a phone can pay without typing a card number.

An SSL certificate encrypts the information that travels between a patient's browser and your website, shown by the padlock in the address bar. We install it and keep it current across the store and checkout.

glossary.d: A type of bank account that allows a business to accept card payments and receive the money from those sales.
The final pages of an online store where the buyer enters a shipping address and payment details and confirms the order.
The card industry's security rules for any business that accepts card payments, which apply to how the payment information is collected and handled.

deliverables.d: A shop section designed with the same colors, fonts and layout as your practice website, so patients know they are still with you.
The part of the store that holds what a patient has chosen, totals the order and walks them through paying for it.
We set up the account that lets your practice accept cards and digital wallets online, with the money deposited to your bank.
One page for each product with photos, a clear description, size options and price, written from the information you give us and approved by you.
An option for patients to receive a product they use regularly on a schedule, charged automatically until they pause or cancel it.
We keep the store online, apply software updates, fix problems and make product or price changes when you send them to us.

fit: you already pay for an EMR with a patient portal but few patients use it
your front desk spends much of the day on refill requests, scheduling calls and paper forms
you are launching or redesigning your website and want the portal built into it from the start
emr-patient-portals.plain: A patient portal is the secure login area that comes with your electronic medical record (EMR) system, where patients can fill out forms, request appointments, ask for refills and see results. This service connects that portal to your practice website, so patients start in one familiar place and are sent to the right portal page for each task. Without that connection, most patients never find the portal and call the front desk instead.

steps.d: We ask which EMR you use, which portal features are turned on and what patients call about most often. You provide a contact at the practice who knows the EMR and the name of your compliance contact.
We map which portal features will appear on the website and where, based on what your EMR allows. You review the plan and confirm with your EMR vendor any features that need to be switched on.

We add the links, pages and instructions, then test each path on phones and computers using a test account or a walkthrough with your staff. Patient information stays inside the portal, and the setup is done with HIPAA requirements in mind and reviewed with your compliance contact.

After your approval we publish the changes and give your front desk a short guide for pointing patients to the website. We check the links periodically and update them when your EMR vendor changes its portal, and you tell us when you add or remove features.

tools.d: The secure patient login area supplied by your EMR vendor, where records, messages and requests are kept. We do not rebuild or replace it, we connect your website to it using the links and options your vendor provides.
The software that runs your website and lets pages be edited without programming, such as WordPress. We use it to add the portal buttons, the resources page and the patient instructions.

A small booking window supplied by many EMR vendors that can sit inside a web page. Where your EMR offers one, we place it on your site so patients request a time without hunting for the right screen.

A tool that counts visits and clicks on your website without identifying individual patients. We use it to see how often the portal links are used and which pages need clearer directions, and we keep tracking limited to the public website.

glossary.d: A setup that lets a person use one username and password to reach more than one system, which some EMR vendors offer and some do not.
A way for two software systems to exchange information automatically, which some EMR vendors make available to connect scheduling or forms to a website.
Any information that can identify a patient and relates to their health, care or payment, which HIPAA requires practices and their vendors to safeguard.

deliverables.d: A clearly labeled patient portal button in your site's menu and on key pages, so patients reach the login in one click.
One page that gathers forms, appointment requests, refill requests and results, each with a short explanation and a direct link to the portal.
Links to your EMR's intake and consent forms, so new patients complete paperwork at home and answers arrive in their chart.
A booking link or embedded scheduler from your EMR, placed where patients look for it, including service pages and the contact page.
Short, plain instructions on creating an account, resetting a password and requesting a refill, written to reduce phone calls to your staff.
A written record of every link, page and setting we added, so your staff and EMR vendor know exactly how things connect.

fit: your phones ring more than your front desk can answer, or callers often reach voicemail after hours
your patients still fill out paper forms on a clipboard in the waiting room and visits start late because of it
you pay for advertising and cannot tell which of it leads to booked appointments
online-booking.plain: Online booking and patient intake is a set of tools on your website that lets a patient pick a visit time and complete their paperwork from a phone, at any hour, without calling your front desk. Many patients choose a practice in the evening or on a weekend, when nobody is there to answer the phone. We connect these tools to the scheduling system you already use, so your staff does not retype anything by hand.

steps.d: We talk through how patients book today and look at the scheduling system you use. You give us a contact at the front desk, your current forms and the name of your compliance contact.

We map each screen a patient will see, from the first button to the final confirmation, and draft the wording of forms and messages. You decide which visit types can be booked online and approve the text.

We install everything and connect it to your scheduling system, then run test bookings with your staff to confirm each one lands in the right place. Your compliance contact reviews any form that collects health information before it goes live.

Once it is live, we watch where patients stop partway through and report which sources produce bookings. You tell us what the front desk is hearing, and we adjust the forms, messages and button placement.

tools.d: This is the software your staff already uses to keep the appointment calendar and patient records. We link online booking to it so new appointments show up there on their own.

This is the free listing that shows your practice in Google Search and Google Maps, with your hours, phone number and reviews. We add a booking link to it so patients can schedule straight from the search results.
These are web forms that protect what a patient types while it is sent and stored. We use them for intake and consent, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact.

This is software that counts visits to your website and records what people do there, without identifying them as patients. We use it to see how many visitors start a booking, how many finish and where they came from.

glossary.d: A connection between two software systems that lets them pass information to each other automatically, so nobody has to enter it twice.
A contract, often shortened to BAA, that HIPAA requires between a practice and any outside company that handles patient health information on its behalf.
A patient who misses a scheduled appointment without canceling ahead of time, leaving an empty slot in the schedule.

deliverables.d: Clearly labeled buttons on your website, Google Business Profile and social pages that take a patient straight to your booking page.
Depending on your system, patients either send a preferred time for staff to approve or choose an open slot themselves.
Your paper forms rebuilt as phone-friendly versions that patients complete and sign at home before they arrive for the visit.
Text and email messages that confirm each appointment and remind the patient beforehand, sent without anyone on your staff lifting a finger.
For practices offering virtual visits, each booked patient receives a link to join the video appointment from their own device.
A simple report showing which ads, searches or social posts led to booked appointments, so marketing decisions rest on real numbers.

fit: your website was built several years ago and has never been checked for accessibility
you collect appointment requests or intake information online and are not sure where that information goes
your attorney or compliance officer has raised concerns about your website and you need someone to carry out the changes
website-accessibility-compliance.plain: Website accessibility means your site can be used by every patient, including people who rely on a screen reader (software that reads the page aloud), who navigate with a keyboard instead of a mouse, or who have low vision. Compliance work covers the other half: making sure forms, tracking codes and security settings treat patient information carefully. We check your site for both, fix what we find, and work with your compliance officer or attorney on anything that needs a legal decision.

steps.d: We ask how your site is used, which forms collect patient information and who handles compliance at your practice. You give us site access and introduce us to your compliance officer or attorney.

We test your pages with automated scanners and by hand, using a keyboard and a screen reader, and we list every tracking code on the site. You receive the report and tell us if any findings need your compliance contact's input.

We correct the problems, add captions, publish the accessibility statement and adjust forms, tags and privacy pages. Your compliance contact approves the policy wording and any decisions about patient data before they go live.

We recheck the site as pages and videos are added, apply security updates and respond to problems patients report. You forward us any feedback you receive and tell us about planned changes to the site.

tools.d: Software that reads a web page and flags common problems, such as text that is hard to see or images with no description. We use scanners to find issues quickly, then confirm each one by hand because automated tools miss a lot.
Programs that read a website aloud for people who are blind or have low vision. We go through your site with one to hear what those patients hear and fix anything confusing or unreachable.

A control panel that holds the small pieces of code your site uses for advertising and visitor statistics. We use it to see what is collecting information on each page and to remove or restrict tracking where patients share health details.

The notice that tells visitors what your site stores in their browser and lets them accept or decline. We install it and configure it to match your privacy policy and what your compliance contact requires.

glossary.d: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, an internationally recognized set of standards for making websites usable by people with disabilities.
A short written description attached to an image that a screen reader speaks aloud so a patient who cannot see the image knows what it shows.
A small piece of code from an advertising or analytics company that records what visitors do on your site and sends that information back to the company.

deliverables.d: A written review of your current site against the WCAG guidelines, listing each problem in plain language and ranked by how serious it is.
Corrections to color contrast, headings, forms, image descriptions and keyboard navigation so patients with disabilities can read and use every page.
Accurate on-screen text for your videos, so patients who are deaf or hard of hearing can follow what is being said.
A public page that explains your commitment to accessibility and gives patients a simple way to tell you when something does not work.
Contact and intake forms set up with HIPAA requirements in mind, plus a check of tracking codes on pages where patients share health details.
Cookie consent, privacy policy pages, an SSL certificate, regular backups and security updates that keep your site protected and current.

fit: your website still shows old hours, former providers or services you no longer offer because no one has time to update it
you do not know who would fix your site if it went down, was hacked or lost its content
you want one team to call for hosting, updates, changes and questions instead of several separate vendors
website-maintenance.plain: Website security and maintenance is the ongoing care that keeps your practice website online, protected, accurate and quick to load after it launches. A website runs on software that needs regular updates, and practice details such as hours, providers and services change often. A designated team handles all of it for you and makes the changes you request within 24 to 48 hours.

steps.d: We talk through how your website is built, where it is hosted and what has been causing trouble. You tell us who at the practice will send requests and approve changes.
We move the site to our hosting or connect to your current setup, then put backups, security updates and monitoring in place. You provide logins for the website, the domain name and any online store.
You send changes by email or phone, and we complete them within 24 to 48 hours. For anything medical, your team confirms the wording is accurate before it goes live.
We check the site daily, apply updates, fix what breaks and keep improving how it appears in search. You read the reports and tell us what is changing at the practice.

tools.d: This is the software your website is built on, such as WordPress, which lets pages be edited without rebuilding the site. We keep it and its add-ons updated and use it to make your changes.

Hosting is the computer that stores your website and delivers it to visitors, and the SSL certificate is what puts the padlock in the browser's address bar. We manage both, and any form that collects patient information is set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact.
A backup system saves copies of your whole website on a schedule and stores them apart from the live site. If an update goes wrong or the site is attacked, we use a recent copy to bring it back.

These are free Google tools that show how many people visit your site, which pages they read and which searches bring them there. We use them to build your reports and to spot errors Google finds on your pages.
tools.t: Google Analytics and Google Search Console

glossary.d: A small add-on program that gives a website an extra feature, such as an appointment form, and that needs regular updates to stay secure.
The address people type to reach your website, such as yourpractice.com, which is registered and renewed separately from the website itself.
Harmful software that attackers place on a website to steal information, send visitors elsewhere or damage the site.

deliverables.d: We keep your website on a server we monitor, so it stays online and loads quickly for patients, including any online store.
We install software updates that close known security gaps and keep saved copies of your site so it can be restored.
Send us new hours, a new provider, updated photos or a new service page, and we make the change for you.
We look for links, images and pages that have stopped working and fix them before patients or search engines run into them.
We keep refining page titles, descriptions and content so search engines such as Google understand what your practice offers and where.
You receive marketing reports showing how people find and use your site, and our team answers questions and explains the numbers.

fit: you offer procedures patients actively search for and your website does not appear near the top of the results
you are paying for every click on ads and want a steadier, more cost effective source of website visitors
your practice is willing to invest in work that builds gradually and holds its value with ongoing maintenance
search-engine-optimization.plain: Search engine optimization, or SEO, is the ongoing work of making your practice website appear near the top of the results when patients search for the procedures you offer. Patients tend to choose from the first few results they see, so a site that ranks well brings in visitors without a fee for every click. It is not a one-time setup, so our staff works on your website daily.

steps.d: We talk with you about your procedures, your location and the patients you most want to reach. You tell us your priorities and give us access to your current website.
We study how competing practices in your area rank and build your keyword list and content plan. You review the list and confirm it matches the procedures you want to promote.
We adjust the structure, set up the code on every page and write or revise the content. You or a designated clinician approve the medical content before it is published.

We keep adding content, earning links and watching how your pages rank, adjusting as search engines and competitors change. You let us know about new procedures, providers or locations so the site stays current.

tools.d: The search engine most patients use to find a doctor or research a procedure. It is the main place we work to have your pages appear, though the same work helps on other search engines too.

A small block of code, invisible to visitors, that tells search engines plain facts such as your specialty, address and hours. We add it to every page so your practice is described correctly in the results.

Software that shows which words people search for and how many other websites compete for them. We use it to choose terms that real patients use and that your practice has a realistic chance of ranking for.
Software that can draft and analyze text quickly. We use it to assist with research and first drafts, and our staff and physicians review everything before it goes on your site.

glossary.d: The unpaid listings on a search results page, which a search engine orders by how relevant and trustworthy it judges each website to be.
The page name written in a website's code, which appears as the clickable headline of your listing in the search results.
Optimization methods that follow the search engines' published rules, as opposed to shortcuts that can get a website penalized or removed from the results.

deliverables.d: A researched list of the words patients type when looking for your procedures, with a plan for which pages should target each one.
Your pages and menus arranged so that both patients and search engines can find every procedure you offer in a click or two.
Titles, descriptions, image labels and structured data added to every page, so search engines can read what each page covers.
New and improved pages about your procedures, written or reviewed by physicians on our staff so the information is accurate and useful.
Relevant websites linking to yours, earned through honest methods only, which signals to search engines that your site can be trusted.
Illustrated summaries of a procedure or topic that patients find easy to read and that other websites like to share and link to.

fit: you have moved, changed phone numbers or added a location, and old details still appear online
your patients come mostly from the surrounding area and other practices appear above you on the map
you have never claimed your Google profile or are not sure who controls it
local-seo.plain: Local search engine optimization (local SEO) is the work of making your practice appear when someone nearby searches for a doctor, a dentist or a treatment you offer, whether on Google, on Google Maps or in medical directories. Search engines compare your name, address, phone number and hours across many websites, and listings that are missing, duplicated or wrong make them less confident about showing you. We correct those listings first, then build out your profiles and pages so patients in your area can find you and reach you.

steps.d: We ask about your locations, providers, services and the areas you want to draw patients from. You give us your current addresses, phone numbers and hours, plus access to any Google profile you already have.

We search for every existing listing of your practice and fix or remove the ones that are incomplete, duplicated or wrong. You may need to answer a verification call, email or postcard from Google or a directory.

We complete your profiles, submit your details, write the location and service pages and add the contact buttons. You approve the pages before they go live, and anything that connects to online booking or a form is set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact.
We watch for new duplicates and unwanted edits, keep your listings current and share what we see in calls, direction requests and local searches. You tell us when hours, providers or services change.

tools.d: The free listing Google gives every business, which appears as the information panel patients see in search results. We use it as the main record of your practice and update it whenever something changes.
The map app and map results many patients use to find a nearby practice and get directions. We make sure each location has its own entry and that the pin sits at the right address and entrance.

Small labels added to your website's code that tell search engines plainly what your practice is, where it is and when it is open. We add them to your pages so the details match your listings exactly.

Software that can compare and draft text quickly. We use it to help spot inconsistent listings and draft page copy, then our team reviews everything and a physician reviews medical content. It never gives medical advice.

glossary.d: NAP stands for name, address and phone number, and consistency means those three details are written the same way everywhere your practice is listed.
Any mention of your practice's name, address and phone number on another website, such as a directory or a review site.
The small group of businesses that Google shows next to a map at the top of the results for a nearby search.

deliverables.d: A report of every listing we find for your practice, with duplicates removed and wrong details corrected.
Your correct practice details submitted to the major data directories that supply information to maps, apps and voice assistants.
A complete, verified profile with your services, hours, photos and categories, which we keep current as things change.
Profiles on the health directories where patients look up providers, claimed and filled in with accurate information for each practitioner.
A page on your website for each office and main service, written so nearby searches lead to the right page.
Buttons on your pages and profiles that let a patient on a phone call you or request an appointment in one tap.

fit: you have noticed patients mentioning that they looked up their options in ChatGPT or another AI assistant before calling.
your practice already has a working website and some search visibility, and you want to build on that foundation.
you are willing to have your physicians review medical content, since that review is a large part of what makes it trustworthy.
ai-search-optimization.plain: AI search optimization is the work of making your practice easy for AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews to understand and safe for them to recommend. These assistants build their answers from sources they trust, including clearly organized web pages, consistent listings, reviews and mentions on reputable sites. A practice that is hard for them to read is often left out of the answer, even when it ranks well in regular search results.

steps.d: We talk through your specialties, locations and priority procedures, then test how AI assistants answer the questions your patients would ask. You give us access to your website and listings and tell us which services matter most.

We turn the audit into an ordered list of fixes and new content, starting with what is most likely to help. You review the plan and confirm that the facts about your practice and physicians are accurate.

We add the markup, correct the listings and write the content, with AI assisting on drafts and our team editing every piece. Your physicians read and approve the medical content before anything is published.
We keep checking how AI answers mention your practice and refine the work as these systems change. You tell us about new physicians, procedures or locations so your information stays current.

tools.d: These are tools such as ChatGPT and the AI summaries at the top of Google results, which answer a question directly instead of only listing links. We ask them the questions your patients would ask and record what they say about your practice.

This is a standard format of code, invisible to visitors, that describes the content of a page to search engines and AI systems. We add it to your site so your physicians, locations, procedures and reviews are read correctly.

This is the free Google listing that shows your practice in Maps and local results, with your hours, phone number, photos and reviews. We keep it complete and accurate, because it is one of the sources AI systems rely on for local information.

This is the software your website runs on, such as WordPress, which lets pages be added and edited without rebuilding the site. We use it to publish the question-and-answer content and author pages, and to place the structured data.

glossary.d: Another name for this service, used because AI assistants give a direct answer instead of a list of links.
A third name for the same work, where generative refers to AI that writes its own response from many sources.
A source that an AI answer links to or names as the place its information came from, which is one way a practice appears in the answer.

deliverables.d: A written report showing how AI assistants currently describe your practice and your competitors, including what they get wrong or leave out.
Behind-the-scenes labels added to your website that tell AI systems exactly who your physicians are, where you practice and what you offer.
Pages that answer the questions patients ask in their own words, drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by editors and physicians before publishing.
Your practice name, address, phone number, hours and services corrected to match across the directories and profiles that AI systems check.
Pages that show which physician wrote or reviewed your medical content, with training and credentials, so readers and AI systems know who stands behind it.
Regular updates in plain language on whether and how your practice appears in AI answers, and what we plan to adjust next.

fit: you are opening a new location or adding a service and cannot wait for unpaid search results to build
your schedule has open appointments for specific procedures that you want to fill
you want to see which marketing dollars led to actual patient calls and bookings
pay-per-click.plain: Pay-per-click marketing places a short text ad for your practice above the regular search results when someone nearby searches for a service you offer. You pay only when a person clicks the ad, which is where the name comes from. A practice needs it because it reaches patients at the moment they are looking for care, without waiting months for a website to climb the unpaid results.

steps.d: We ask about your services, service area, capacity and the monthly budget you are comfortable with. You tell us which procedures you want more patients for and who should approve ad wording.

We set up the campaigns, keywords, ads and landing pages, and send them to you for review. You give us access to your website and any existing ad account, and confirm that every claim in the ads is accurate.

We turn the ads on and connect call and booking tracking, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact. Your front desk only needs to answer the phone and handle requests as usual.
We review the search terms, adjust bids, test new ad wording and move budget toward what brings in patients. You tell us when your schedule, services or priorities change so the campaigns can follow.

tools.d: This is the platform where businesses pay to show ads on Google search results. We build and manage your campaigns inside it, and the account stays in your practice's name.
These are phone numbers that forward to your regular line and record which ad led to the call. We place them on your ads and landing pages so every call can be traced to its source.
Analytics software counts what visitors do on your website after they arrive. We use it to see which ads lead to completed booking forms and which lead to visitors leaving.

These are software programs that can draft and reword text quickly. We use them to draft ad variations and sort search data, and our team reviews everything before it runs, with physician review for medical content.

glossary.d: The amount you pay each time someone clicks your ad, which varies with how many other advertisers want the same search phrase.
A rating Google gives each keyword based on how well your ad and landing page match the search, which affects your position and cost.
A visitor taking the action you want, such as calling the office or submitting an appointment request.

deliverables.d: Your account is arranged into separate campaigns for each service, so spending and results for each one stay easy to read.
We divide your monthly ad spend among your services according to which ones matter most to your practice right now.
A researched list of the phrases patients type when looking for your services, plus phrases we block to avoid wasted clicks.
Several versions of each ad, drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by our team so the wording is accurate and appropriate.
Each campaign gets its own web page that matches the ad and gives visitors one clear way to call or book.
Regular reports show how many phone calls and appointment requests the ads produced, not only how many people clicked.

fit: your market is crowded and competing practices already appear above you in search results
you are opening a location or adding a service and cannot wait for unpaid rankings to build
you have a set monthly ad budget and front desk staff ready to answer new inquiries promptly
search-engine-marketing.plain: Paid advertising places your practice at the top of Google search results and in the feeds of people on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok, and you pay the platform each time someone clicks or views your ad. Unpaid search rankings (SEO) build slowly and may not be enough in a crowded market, so paid ads put you in front of patients as soon as a campaign starts. We can set up the account and teach your team to run it, or manage it for you.

steps.d: We ask about your services, your area, your competitors and what you want the ads to achieve. You tell us which treatments matter most and what monthly ad budget you are comfortable with.

We build the accounts, structure the campaigns and connect them to your website so results can be measured. You give us website access, and anything that touches patient data is set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact.
We produce the ads and check them against each platform's rules for health and aesthetic advertising. You review and approve the wording, images and offers before anything goes live.

We watch where the budget goes and move it toward the ads that bring inquiries, much as a broker manages a portfolio. You tell us which inquiries became patients, or your trained staff takes over the account with us available for questions.

tools.d: Google's system for buying the sponsored listings that appear above the regular search results. We use it to show your practice when someone nearby searches a phrase such as "Botox Fort Lauderdale".

Paid posts and videos that appear in people's feeds and stories, managed from one shared advertising account. We use them to reach people by location and interests, and they often cost less per click than search.

Short paid videos that appear between the regular videos people scroll through on TikTok. We use them mainly for aesthetic and wellness services, where a brief, visual introduction to the practice works well.

Software that helps draft many versions of an ad, with different headlines, images and wording, and compares how each performs. Our team reviews every version before it runs and keeps the ones that bring inquiries.

glossary.d: The most you agree to pay for one click on your ad, which the platform weighs against other advertisers to decide whose ad is shown.
A group of new people the platform finds because they resemble your best existing patients, built without sharing health information.
The action you want a person to take after clicking an ad, such as calling the office or submitting a booking request.

deliverables.d: Accounts on Google and the social platforms, set up in your practice's name so the account and its history stay yours.
A written list of the search phrases we will bid on and the groups of people each social campaign will reach.
The written ads, images and short videos for each platform, drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by our team before anything runs.
Follow-up ads shown to people who visited your website but did not book, keeping your practice in view while they decide.
Short campaigns built around promotions, new services or events, planned ahead so they start and stop on the dates you choose.
Either working sessions that teach your staff to create ads and maintain the account, or regular management and plain-language reports from us.

fit: you provide good care but have only a handful of reviews, or most of them are several years old
your front desk has no time to ask for reviews or to check several sites for new ones
you are unsure how to answer a negative review without saying anything about the patient
reputation-management.plain: Reviews and reputation management is the ongoing work of asking patients for reviews, replying to the ones you receive and keeping your public listings correct. Patients usually read what others say about a practice before they call, and search engines and AI assistants use reviews as one of the signals for which practices to show. We run the process for you so it happens after every visit, not only when someone on your staff has a free moment.

steps.d: We look at where your practice is listed, what patients have written and what is out of date. You give us access to your Google Business Profile and other listings, or we help you claim them.

We write the request messages and decide with you when they go out after a visit. Because this uses patient contact details, it is set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact.
We settle the tone of your replies and who approves them. You name one person at the practice who can read drafts and say yes or ask for changes.
Requests go out, we watch for new reviews, draft replies and keep your profile updated. You approve replies and tell us about changes such as new hours, providers or services.

tools.d: This is the free listing that shows your practice in Google Search and Google Maps, with your rating, hours and photos. We manage it on your behalf and keep its details accurate.
This is software that gathers reviews from many sites into one place and sends the requests to patients. We set it up, connect your listings and handle it day to day.
These are the two channels patients are most likely to see shortly after an appointment. We use them to send one polite request with a link that opens the review form directly.

These are programs that can write a first version of a text from instructions. AI drafts the replies, then our team reviews and edits each one before it reaches you for approval, and it never gives medical advice.

glossary.d: The practice of asking only satisfied patients for public reviews, which review sites prohibit and which we do not do.
The average of all scores patients have given your practice on a site, shown as one to five stars next to your name.
The page a site such as Google, Healthgrades or Yelp keeps about your practice, showing your name, address, phone number and reviews.

deliverables.d: Each patient receives a short text or email after the appointment with a direct link to leave a review.
Reviews from Google, Healthgrades, Yelp and other sites appear on a single screen, so nobody has to check each site separately.
We write a reply to each review for you to approve, worded so it never reveals or confirms any patient information.
We keep your Google listing current with accurate hours, services, photos and regular posts, so patients find correct information when they search.
You get a notification when a review needs attention, such as a low rating or a complaint, so it is not left unanswered.
Your published reviews are shown on your own site, where visitors can read them while deciding whether to book an appointment.

fit: your front desk regularly misses calls while helping the patients standing in front of them
you receive inquiries on evenings and weekends and nobody is available to respond until the next business day
you serve Spanish-speaking patients and do not always have a bilingual staff member available to answer
ai-chat-messaging.plain: AI agents are software assistants that answer patients on your website chat, your text line and your phone when your staff cannot, including at lunch and after hours. They answer common questions using only the information you approve, take booking requests and pass the conversation to your team when a person is needed. A practice needs this because a patient who gets no answer often calls the next practice on the list.

steps.d: We meet with you to understand how patients reach you today and where calls and messages go unanswered. You provide your services, hours, locations, policies and the questions your front desk hears most.

AI drafts the answers and our team edits them, then you and your physicians review and approve every one before it is used. Clinical questions are marked to go straight to your staff, because the agents never give medical advice or diagnose.

We connect the agents to your website, phone line and text number, working with your compliance contact so the setup is done with HIPAA requirements in mind. Your staff tries real scenarios and tells us what to correct before patients see anything.
After launch, we send reports on what patients ask most and where the agents had to pass a conversation to a person. You tell us what has changed in the practice, and we update the answers.

tools.d: These are the programs that understand a question written or spoken in everyday language and compose a reply. We restrict them to your approved information, so they answer from your policies and not from the open internet.

This is technology that turns a caller's speech into text, finds the right answer and speaks it back in a natural voice. We set it to pick up after hours and to send any urgent or clinical call to the path you choose.

This is a text line tied to your practice number, which lets software send and receive messages on your behalf. We use it for missed-call replies, reminders and follow-ups, with patient consent and opt-out handled properly.

These are the connections between the agents and the systems you already use, such as your phone service and appointment calendar. We use them so booking requests and call notes arrive where your staff already works.

glossary.d: The collection of approved facts about your practice, such as services, prices and policies, that an agent is allowed to draw its answers from.
The moment an agent stops and transfers a conversation to a human staff member because the question is clinical, sensitive or outside its approved answers.
A written record of everything said between a patient and an agent, which your staff can read before they respond.

deliverables.d: A chat window on your site that answers questions about services, hours and locations, and collects booking requests for your front desk.
When a call goes unanswered, the caller receives a text from your practice within seconds, so the conversation continues instead of ending.
A phone assistant that picks up when the office is closed, speaks English and Spanish, and records what each caller needs.
Automatic text messages that remind patients of upcoming appointments and check in afterward, which saves your staff from making those calls by hand.
Whenever a person is needed, your team receives the full conversation, so nobody has to ask the patient to repeat themselves.
Call summaries for your manager, draft replies to reviews and messages for your approval, and a private assistant that answers new staff questions.

fit: you know your practice should be active on social media but nobody on staff has the time to do it consistently
your profiles exist but have not been updated in months and no longer reflect the practice
you offer elective or cash-pay services that patients research and compare online before choosing a provider
social-media.plain: Social media management means a dedicated team plans, writes, designs and publishes posts on your practice's social networks, and answers the people who respond to them. Patients look for health information and get a feel for a practice on these networks long before they call, so a quiet or outdated profile can cost you their trust. You do not have to use social media yourself for it to work for your practice.

steps.d: We talk with you about your goals, services and ideal patients, then study the networks and practices in your market. You tell us which procedures matter most and who should approve content.
We create or update your accounts and prepare the first batch of posts. You provide account access, your logo, photos of the office and team, and any rules your compliance contact wants followed.
We publish the first posts and turn on any agreed ads. You review and approve the opening content so the tone sounds like your practice.
We post every week, respond to your audience and report what is getting attention. You send us news, events and signed patient consent for any photos or stories we use.

tools.d: The two networks where most patients browse photos, short videos and local business pages. We publish your posts here and answer the comments and messages they bring in.
A program that lets posts be prepared in advance and published automatically at set times. We use it to keep your accounts active every week without anyone at the practice having to log in.

Software that can draft text and suggest ideas from a short instruction. We use it to draft captions and topic lists, then our writers edit them and a physician reviews anything medical before it goes out.
The paid side of the networks, where a post can be shown to people by location, age or interests. We use them to put your events and services in front of nearby people who do not follow you yet.

glossary.d: The total of likes, comments, shares and saves a post receives, which shows whether people actually paid attention to it.
The number of different people who saw a post at least once, whether or not they follow you.
The moment a viewer takes the action you wanted, such as calling the office or filling out an appointment request form.

deliverables.d: A short plan that names which networks you will use, who you are trying to reach and what topics you will cover.
A summary of what similar practices in your area post and where patients in your specialty spend time online.
Your accounts set up or cleaned up with correct contact details, logo, photos and a consistent description of your practice.
Original photos, short videos and captions published every week, drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by our team and a physician.
We watch your comments and messages, reply to routine questions and pass anything clinical or sensitive to your staff.
Paid campaigns for events, new services or special offers, with booking links adjusted so more viewers become appointment requests.

fit: you are comfortable speaking on camera for a few minutes at a time, or willing to try with our guidance
your patients ask the same questions again and again, and you would like to answer them once in a way many people can see
your practice has social media accounts that nobody on staff has the time to film or post for
short-form-video.plain: Short-form videos are vertical clips, usually under a minute, that people watch on their phones on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and Facebook. For many patients, one of these clips is the first time they see and hear a doctor, and it shapes whether they feel comfortable booking. We plan, film, edit and publish these videos for your practice so you only need to show up for the filming.

steps.d: We talk with you and your staff about your services and the questions patients ask, then send a content plan for the month. You review it and tell us what to add, remove or avoid.

We come to your office and film everything in one session, guiding you through each topic so you do not need a script. You provide a block of time, a quiet room and, for any patient who appears on camera, their signed consent.

We edit the footage, with AI assisting on the first cuts and our editors finishing the work, and our physician advisory board reviews the medical claims. You approve the final videos before anything goes public.
We post the approved videos on each network on a regular schedule and report on how they performed. You tell us what patients mention at the front desk, and we use both to shape the next plan.

tools.d: These are the short video sections of Instagram and Facebook, where clips are shown to people nearby and to people interested in a topic, not only to your followers. We publish your videos here with a description and location details that fit your practice.

A phone app built entirely around short videos, which many people now use to look up health topics and local providers. We post versions of your videos formatted for it, so you do not need to learn the app yourself.

The short video section of YouTube, which is owned by Google, so these clips can also appear when people search for a topic. We upload your videos here with clear titles based on the question each one answers.

Editing programs that use AI to transcribe speech, draft captions and suggest where to cut a long recording into shorter clips. We use them to speed up the routine work, and our editors and physician reviewers check every video before it is published.

glossary.d: A short vertical video, made to fill a phone screen, that social networks show to people who may not follow you yet.
The first second or two of a video, where a clear question or statement gives the viewer a reason to keep watching.
Taking one recording and editing it into several different videos or lengths so a single filming session goes further.

deliverables.d: A list of video topics for the month, drawn from the questions your patients and front desk hear most often.
Our crew films at your office in a single visit, recording enough short answers and clips to cover several weeks of posts.
Each clip is trimmed, cleaned up and given on-screen captions so viewers can follow along with the sound off.
Every video gets a still image with a clear title, so your profile looks organized and people can find a topic quickly.
AI-assisted editing helps us cut the same recording into different lengths and versions, and our editors check each one before it is used.
We post each video on every network for you and send a report showing which topics people watched, saved and shared.

fit: you have years of patient email addresses in your records and rarely or never write to them
your patients come in for one treatment and often do not know about the other services you offer
you want to stay in regular contact with patients but nobody on your staff has time to write and send emails
e-mail-marketing.plain: Email marketing management is a regular, planned flow of emails from your practice to your patients: newsletters, occasional promotions, event invitations and automatic messages such as a welcome note or a birthday greeting. We run the whole operation for you, from the patient list to the writing, sending and reporting. Patients who hear from you with useful information remember who you are, what you offer and how to reach you when they are ready to book.

steps.d: We talk through your services, your patients and how often you want to send. You provide your current patient contact list, your brand materials and the name of your compliance contact, so that patient data is handled with HIPAA requirements in mind.

We prepare the list, design the templates, build the automatic emails and configure your sending domain so messages are recognized as coming from you. You approve the designs and confirm which patient groups make sense for your practice.
AI helps us draft and organize, our physicians write and review the medical content, and our team prepares each email. You review the calendar and can edit or decline anything before it is sent.

We send on the agreed schedule and report on who opened, who clicked and which bookings each campaign produced. We use those results to adjust topics and timing, and you tell us about new services or events to include.

tools.d: This is the software that stores your contact list, sends email to many people at once and records what happens to each message. We set it up and manage it for you, so your staff does not need to learn it.

These are settings on your web domain that prove to Gmail, Outlook and other providers that an email really comes from your practice. We configure them so your messages are more likely to reach the inbox and not the spam folder.

These are short forms on your website where a visitor types an email address to request a free report. We build them into your site and connect them to your list, so each new contact is saved and receives the report automatically.

These are software tools that can draft and summarize text. We use them to assist with drafts and subject line ideas, and every email is reviewed by our team and by physicians before it is sent; AI never gives medical advice to your patients.

glossary.d: Dividing your contact list into groups, for example by treatment received or stated interest, so each group gets emails that apply to them.
A measure of whether your emails actually arrive in the inbox, as opposed to being blocked or sent to spam.
The share of recipients who opened an email and the share who clicked a link inside it, which together show how much interest a message produced.

deliverables.d: We set up your contact list, remove bad or duplicate addresses and group patients by treatment and interest so messages stay relevant.
We design reusable email layouts with your logo, colors and contact details, so every message looks like it came from your practice.
Our physicians write and review informative newsletters for your patients, and you can read, change or approve each one before it goes out.
You receive a monthly plan showing which newsletters, promotions and event invitations go out and when, at the interval you choose.
We build emails that send themselves at the right moment: a welcome series, post-visit follow-up, birthday greetings and notes to patients who have not returned.
Visitors enter their email address to receive a free physician-written report, such as one on healthy skin, and join your list.

fit: you have open appointment slots that often go unfilled on short notice.
your patients come back for repeat treatments and tend to forget when the next one is due.
you already send emails and want a faster channel for time-sensitive announcements.
sms-marketing.plain: SMS campaign management is the planning, writing, sending and tracking of text messages to patients who have agreed to hear from your practice. Because texts are usually read within minutes, they suit time-sensitive news such as an open appointment this week or a seasonal offer. Mobile carriers and consent laws set strict rules for business texting, and we handle those rules so your messages get through and your practice stays within them.

steps.d: We talk through your services, slow periods and how you collect patient phone numbers today. You tell us who answers messages at the front desk and who your compliance contact is.
We submit your business details to the carriers and build your sign-up forms and messaging account. You provide your legal business name, tax ID and practice address, which the carriers ask for.

AI helps us draft each message, our writers edit it, and a physician reviews anything that touches on treatments. Nothing is sent until you or your practice manager approve the wording and the send date.
We send the campaigns, watch the replies and share the results with you. Each round shows us which messages and send times your patients respond to, and we adjust the next campaign accordingly.

tools.d: This is the software that stores your contact list, sends texts in bulk and records every reply and stop request. We set it up, run it for you and give you access to see everything that goes out.

This is the industry process where a business identifies itself and describes the kind of messages it plans to send. We prepare and submit the application for your practice and respond to any questions the carriers raise.

These are programs that can draft text and answer simple written questions. We use them to prepare first drafts for our writers and to power the reply agent, which covers hours, directions and booking and never gives medical advice.

This is the system your office already uses for appointments and patient contact details. Where it can connect to the texting platform, we link the two with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact involved.

glossary.d: The standard ten-digit local phone number that businesses register with carriers in order to send text messages to customers.
The Telephone Consumer Protection Act, the federal law that requires a business to have a person's permission before sending them marketing texts.
The late evening and early morning period when marketing texts should not be sent, based on the time zone of the person receiving them.

deliverables.d: Your practice's texting number is registered with the mobile carriers, which is required before business messages can be delivered reliably.
Sign-up forms and a join word patients can text, plus a dated record showing that each person agreed to receive messages.
Promotions, event invitations and last-minute openings written by us, approved by you and sent at a time patients are likely to respond.
Texts that go out on their own when a repeat treatment is due or after a visit, without health details in the message.
Patient replies go to your front desk or to an AI agent that handles routine questions and passes anything clinical to your staff.
A plain summary after each campaign showing how many patients replied, how many booked and how many asked to stop receiving texts.

fit: you know your website needs more and better writing, but no one in the office has time to do it
you have collected patient email addresses and are not sending them anything on a regular basis
your current website firm expects you or your staff to supply the articles and blog posts
physician-content-marketing.plain: Physician content marketing is the written material that represents your practice online: the pages of your website, blog posts, articles, press releases and the newsletters emailed to your patients. Patients and search engines both judge a practice by what it publishes, and AI assistants now quote websites directly, so the writing has to be clear, current and medically accurate. Physicians write or review the medical content, our internet writers prepare it for the web, and your staff is not asked to write anything.

steps.d: We talk with you about your services, your patients and what you want to be known for. You provide basic information about the practice, your physicians and any topics you want covered or avoided.

We put together a list of pages, articles and newsletter subjects based on what patients search for and what your practice offers. You look over the list and tell us if anything is missing or off the mark.

Our writers research and draft with the help of AI tools, a physician writes or reviews the medical content, and our internet staff makes it search engine friendly. You do not need to write, and you can read pieces before they go out if you wish.

We post the content to your website, send the newsletters to your patient list and keep adding new material on a regular schedule. Your part is to tell us about news at the practice, such as a new service or physician.

tools.d: This is the software behind your website that lets pages and blog posts be added or changed without rebuilding the site. We use it to publish and update your content, so your staff never has to log in.

This is a service that stores a list of email addresses and sends the same message to everyone on it, with a way to unsubscribe. We use it to send your newsletters to the addresses your website collects, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact.

These are computer programs that can research a topic and produce a first draft of text quickly. We use them to assist our writers, and a physician checks medical content before it is published, so nothing goes out on AI output alone.

Google and similar search engines, along with AI assistants that answer questions by quoting websites, are how many patients first read about a practice. We write and format your content so these systems can read it easily and represent it accurately.

glossary.d: The work of making a website easier for search engines such as Google to find, understand and show to people looking for what you offer.
The process by which a search engine reads a web page and adds it to its records so the page can appear in search results.
A list of email addresses from people who have agreed to receive messages from your practice.

deliverables.d: Pages about your practice, physicians and services, written from the information you give us so they describe your practice accurately.
Fresh pages and updates added as part of ongoing maintenance, so readers see current information and search engines have something new to index.
Physician-written newsletters emailed to the patients on your list, keeping your practice familiar until they are ready to book a visit.
Educational pieces on the topics your patients ask about, published under your practice name to help people find you through search.
Short announcements about news at your practice, such as a new physician, location or service, written and published for you.
Every piece with medical content is written or checked by a physician before it is published, including anything first drafted with AI tools.

fit: you have happy patients who would gladly speak about their experience but nothing on your website that shows them
your website describes your services well but feels impersonal to someone visiting for the first time
you offer elective or aesthetic services where new patients want to hear from someone who has already been through it
video-testimonials.plain: A medical video testimonial is a short, professionally filmed video in which your real patients describe, in their own words, what it was like to be cared for at your practice. Our videographers come to your office, interview the patients who volunteer and edit the footage into a finished video for your website. New visitors tend to trust a person they can see and hear more than a written quote, which makes them more comfortable contacting you.

steps.d: We talk with you about your practice, the services you want to highlight and a filming date that will not disrupt your schedule. You tell us which rooms we can use and who our day-of contact will be.

You invite satisfied patients who are willing to appear on camera and collect their written permission. This step is set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact.
Our crew arrives, sets up in the space you have chosen and interviews each volunteer in turn. You only need to keep that space available and have your patients arrive at their scheduled times.

Our editors build the final video and send it to you with the files. Once you confirm it represents your practice accurately, it goes on your website, where it keeps working for you with every new visitor.

tools.d: This is the filming equipment that captures a sharp picture and clear voices, even in a busy office. We bring and operate all of it, so you do not need to buy or rent anything.
These are the programs editors use to cut, arrange and polish raw footage. We use them to correct sound and color, add your practice name and logo, and shape the interviews into one finished piece.

This is an online service, such as YouTube or Vimeo, that stores a video and plays it smoothly on any phone or computer. The finished video can be stored there so it loads quickly on your website without slowing your pages down.

This is a small piece of behind-the-scenes code that tells search engines like Google that a page contains a video and what it is about. It can be added to the page that holds your testimonial, so the video supports your search engine optimization.

glossary.d: Extra footage of your office, staff and surroundings that is shown while a patient is speaking to make the video more interesting to watch.
A signed form in which a patient gives written permission for their image, voice and story to be used in your marketing.
Placing a video on a web page so visitors can press play and watch it there without leaving your site.

deliverables.d: Our videographers travel to your office and spend half a day filming, so patients and staff stay in familiar surroundings.
Our experienced interviewers put your volunteers at ease and ask simple questions, so their answers sound natural instead of rehearsed.
We also film your office itself, giving future patients a look at the place before they ever walk in.
Our editors select the strongest moments, trim the pauses and combine everything into one clear, well-paced story.
You receive a polished video of real patients describing their experience, ready to place on your website.
The video files and final product are yours to keep, and everything is covered by one all-inclusive fee.

fit: you pay for advertising and cannot say with confidence which inquiries turned into booked patients
your front desk is too busy during clinic hours to answer every new inquiry within minutes
your treatments are repeated on a schedule and patients often drift away without a reminder
patient-crm-automation.plain: A patient CRM (customer relationship management system) is one place that holds every person who has contacted your practice, what they asked about and what happened next. Lead management is the routine built around it: each new inquiry gets a fast reply, a series of follow-ups and a clear status until the person books or declines. Practices need it because most inquiries are lost through slow or forgotten follow-up, not through bad marketing.

steps.d: We review how inquiries reach you today and who answers them. You tell us your services, office hours, booking rules and who your compliance contact is.

We set up the CRM and connect it to your website, ads and call tracking, with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact involved. You provide logins and, if you want, a list of past patients to import.

We draft the replies, follow-up sequences and reminders, with AI assisting and our team reviewing every message. You approve the wording and decide whether first responses come from your staff, our team or an AI agent.

We monitor the system, send your weekly report and adjust messages, scoring and routing based on what the numbers show. Your staff keeps each lead's status up to date and tells us when services or offers change.

tools.d: Software that stores every lead and patient contact with a full history of messages, calls and appointments. We configure it for your practice, train your staff and maintain it.

Phone numbers assigned to specific ads or pages that forward to your regular line and record which source produced each call. We use them to credit phone inquiries to the right campaign inside the CRM.

Rules that send a prepared message when something happens, such as a form being submitted or a set number of months passing since a visit. We use it for first replies, follow-ups, treatment reminders and reactivation campaigns.

Software that can answer a new inquiry by text or chat at any hour, ask basic questions and offer appointment times. Ours follow scripts you approve, never give medical advice and hand the conversation to a person when a question goes beyond scheduling.

glossary.d: A person who has contacted your practice or shared their contact details but has not yet booked an appointment.
A visual board showing where each person stands, from first inquiry to consultation booked to treatment done.
The practice of tracing a booked patient back to the specific ad, search or post that first brought them to you.

deliverables.d: Web forms, phone calls, texts, website chat and social media messages arrive in a single screen, so nothing sits unseen in a separate account.
Each inquiry is labeled with the ad, campaign or page that produced it, so you know which marketing brings actual patients.
New inquiries receive an immediate reply, then a planned series of messages over the following days until they book or opt out.
