Inquiries are ranked by how ready the person appears to book and sent to the right staff member, so the best ones get called first.
Past patients receive reminders when a repeat treatment is due, plus birthday, promotion and event messages, and a note if they have been away.
A short report each week shows how many leads came in, were contacted, booked or were lost, with the reason for each loss.

fit: you recently completed a course in a new procedure and have not yet told your patients about it
your practice has room in the schedule for the new service and staff ready to answer questions about it
you want one team to handle the website, the announcements, the ads and the printed materials together
new-service-launch.plain: A service launch is a coordinated plan that takes a procedure you have just trained in and makes it visible and bookable for patients. A new skill does not fill appointments on its own, because your current patients and the people in your area do not yet know you offer it. We prepare the pages, the announcements, the advertising and the in-office materials together, so the first bookings arrive while your training is still fresh.

steps.d: We talk through the procedure you trained in, who it is for in your practice, your capacity and the first month you want to fill. You tell us about your equipment, your schedule and any offer you have in mind.

We write and design the pages, messages, ads and printed materials, with AI assisting the drafts and our team and a physician reviewing them. You record a few short videos, check the medical content and approve everything before it goes out.
We announce the service to your current patients first, then turn on the campaigns in your area. Your front desk uses the script we provide to answer questions and book the requests that come in.
We report which channels produced inquiries and bookings, and we shift effort toward what is working. You tell us how the appointments are going so the message matches what patients experience.

tools.d: A landing page is a single web page built around one treatment and one action, which is requesting an appointment. We send ad visitors there so they are not distracted by the rest of your website.

These are services that send one message to many patients at once and show who opened it. We use them for your announcement, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and together with your practice's compliance contact.

These are paid placements on Google search results and on platforms such as Instagram and Facebook. We limit them to your area so your budget goes to people who could realistically become your patients.
tools.t: Google Ads and social media ads

tools.d: This is a way of recording which ad, email or page led to each form request or phone call. We use it to show you what the launch returned on the training you paid for.

glossary.d: The single next step a page or message asks the reader to take, such as requesting a consultation.
The moment a visitor does what the page was built for, for example submitting the booking form or calling the office.
Setting an ad campaign to appear only to people in a chosen area, such as the neighborhoods around your practice.

deliverables.d: A permanent page on your website plus a focused page for ad visitors, both with content reviewed by a physician before publishing.
A clear opening offer for the new procedure and a simple online form so interested patients can request an appointment right away.
Messages to the patients you already have, who trust you and are usually the first to book a new treatment.
Paid ads shown to people in your area who are searching for the treatment or likely to be interested in it.
Brief clips of you explaining the treatment in your own words, used on your pages, social profiles and ads.
Brochures, posters, a front desk script, consent forms and pre and post treatment instructions, all for your review and approval.

fit: you are opening a practice or adding a location and want a plan before you spend on marketing
you already pay for a website, ads or social media and cannot tell which of them brings in patients
your practice has grown by referrals and you now want a steadier, more predictable flow of new patients
marketing-strategy.plain: A marketing strategy is a written plan that says where your practice should spend its marketing money and effort, in what order, and how you will know whether it is working. Without one, practices tend to buy services one at a time, such as a new website here and some ads there, with no way to tell which of them brings in patients. Our business staff builds the plan around your specialty and your local competitors, and our physician advisory board adds what physicians know about how patients choose a doctor.

steps.d: We ask about your specialty, your goals, the procedures you want more of and what you have tried before. You tell us your rough budget and who on your team will be our main contact.

We study your current marketing and your competitors. You give us view-only access to your website statistics, ad accounts and business listing, or we work from what is publicly visible if you have none of these.
We present the audit, the priorities, the budget and the 90-day roadmap in one meeting. You decide what to approve and who on your side owns each task assigned to the practice.
We meet each month to compare results against the plan and adjust it. You share what the reports cannot show, such as how many inquiries became booked appointments.

tools.d: Software that counts how many people visit your website, where they came from and what they did there. We use it to see which marketing efforts send visitors who go on to call or request an appointment.
The free listing that shows your practice name, hours, photos and reviews in Google Search and Google Maps. We check how complete it is and how it compares with the listings of practices near you.

Phone numbers that forward to your front desk and record which ad or web page prompted each call. Where the plan recommends them, they are set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact.

Software that can read and summarize large amounts of text quickly. AI assists us in sorting through competitor websites and patient review themes, and our staff and physicians review everything before it reaches your plan.

glossary.d: Any single route by which patients find you, such as Google search, paid ads, social media, email or referrals.
The moment a person takes the action you want, such as calling the office or submitting an appointment request.
The amount spent on marketing divided by the number of people who contacted the practice as a result.

deliverables.d: A written review of your website, search rankings, ads, patient reviews and nearby competitors, showing what is working and what is not.
A ranked list of the marketing channels worth your money, with a suggested budget for each one and the reasoning behind it.
A calendar of tasks for the next 90 days, each with a named owner and a due date so nothing stalls.
A meeting each month where we go through the numbers with you and agree on what to keep, stop or change.
Comments from practicing physicians on your plan, covering how patients in your specialty typically compare and choose a provider.
Direct access to our business and marketing staff for questions on hiring, vendors, new services or anything else the plan raises.

fit: you are opening a new practice or location and need a logo and printed materials from scratch
your current brochures, cards and signs were made at different times and no longer match each other
you want to encourage patient referrals and need something professional for staff to hand out
medical-graphic-design.plain: Medical branding and graphic design is the work of creating your practice's visual identity: an original logo, a set of colors and typefaces, and the printed pieces patients actually hold, such as brochures and postcards. A practice needs it because patients judge professionalism by what they see, and mismatched materials from different vendors make a good practice look disorganized. We design and write everything as one matching set, so your front desk handouts, mailers and social media graphics all look like they come from the same place.

steps.d: We ask about your specialty, your patients, your budget and the look you like or dislike. You send us any existing logo, photos, provider bios and a list of the services you want to feature.
Our designers present logo options with matching colors and type, and you tell us what to keep and what to change. Once you approve a direction, it becomes the basis for every other piece.

We write the brochure and postcard text, lay out each piece and send you proofs to review. You check names, credentials, services, promotions and contact details for accuracy before anything is finalized.

We deliver final files ready for a print shop and for online use, organized so your staff can find them. When you add a provider, a service or a promotion, we update the affected pieces in the same style.

tools.d: Professional drawing programs that build a logo from shapes instead of pixels, so it stays sharp at any size from a business card to an outdoor sign. Our designers use them to create your logo and lay out your printed pieces.

Software that can draft text and suggest visual ideas quickly. We use it to assist with first drafts and early concepts, then our designers and writers refine the work, and physicians review any medical content before you see it.

The standard file format print shops accept, with the correct size, margins and color settings built in. We prepare one for each piece so you can send it to the printer of your choice without extra setup.
An online folder that holds your logo files, style guide and templates in one place. We organize it so your staff, your printer and any future vendor all work from the same approved versions.

glossary.d: The combination of logo, colors, typefaces and layout style that makes your practice recognizable wherever it appears.
A preview of a design sent for your review and approval before it is printed or published.
A small extra margin of color or image beyond the edge of a printed piece, trimmed off so no white border shows.

deliverables.d: A logo designed only for your practice, delivered in the formats needed for signs, print, your website and social media.
A short document listing your exact colors, typefaces and logo rules so anyone producing materials for you keeps them consistent.
A custom brochure covering your credentials, background and services, written by our staff and designed with your logo and practice details.
Single-topic brochures that explain one service to interested patients, with text our physician staff can write and you approve.
Handouts your staff give to patients to pass along to friends and family, describing your credentials, services and current promotions.
A 6×9 postcard listing your services and contact details, plus stationery, business cards, posters, displays or social media graphics as needed.

fit: you are opening a new location or adding a service and need printed materials ready for patients
your brochures, cards and signs were made at different times by different vendors and no longer look alike
you want to reach households near your practice by mail without managing a printer and a mailing service yourself
printing.plain: Printing and fulfillment means the paper side of your practice, such as brochures, cards, posters and mailers, is designed, printed and delivered to your office by one team. Print still does work a screen cannot: a brochure goes home with the patient, and a referral card travels to a friend. Because the same people handle your design and your printing, the colors and logos on paper match your website.

steps.d: We talk through what you need, how many, and where each piece will be used. You tell us the services to feature and send any existing logo files, photos or wording.

We lay out each piece and prepare the text, with AI assisting on drafts and our team reviewing everything, including physician review of medical content. You confirm that details such as hours, addresses and provider names are correct.
We send a proof for you to review and mark up. Once you approve it, the files go to the same print partner that produces Empire Medical Training's materials.

The finished pieces arrive at your door, or go out in the mail if it is a direct mail campaign. We keep your files on hand, so when supplies run low you ask for a reorder or an update instead of starting over.

tools.d: The professional programs used to arrange text, photos and logos on a page at exact print sizes. We use them to build each piece so it matches the look of your website.

Software that can draft and tighten text quickly. We use it to prepare first drafts of brochure and care sheet wording, and then our writers and a physician review and correct every piece before you see it.

The industrial equipment at our print partner that produces everything from small batches of cards to large banners. The press type and paper are matched to each job, so you do not have to choose them yourself.

Postcards or letters sent through the postal service to chosen addresses or whole neighborhoods. We print, address and mail them for you, and if a mailing would use your own patient list, we set that up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your practice's compliance contact.

glossary.d: A final preview of a printed piece, sent to you to check and approve before the full quantity is printed.
A tall, narrow card printed on sturdy paper, made to sit in a display stand at a front desk or waiting room.
Thick, stiff paper used for business cards, postcards and appointment cards so they hold up to handling.

deliverables.d: Layouts for each piece, built with your logo, colors and wording, and sized correctly so they print cleanly the first time.
A preview of every piece that you check for wording, phone numbers and colors, and nothing goes to press until you sign off.
Practice and procedure brochures, before and after care sheets, and menus of services or price lists that patients can take home and read.
Business cards, appointment cards, referral cards, rack cards, gift and loyalty cards, plus letterhead, envelopes and folders that all share one look.
Exam room posters, window graphics, banners and event displays that introduce your services to people in your office or at community events.
Finished pieces are shipped to your office, or postcards are printed, addressed and mailed to the neighborhoods around your practice.

fit: you are opening a new practice or location and need the website, print materials and forms in place together
your current website looks fine but brings in few new patient inquiries, and your printed materials do not match it
you are adding aesthetic or elective procedures and your front desk has not been trained to handle calls from patients comparing providers
medical-practice-kit.plain: The medical practice marketing kit is a complete marketing program in one package: a custom website built so patients can find you in search results, the printed materials for your office, a training manual for your front desk, and the consent and treatment forms for your procedures. A practice needs all of these to work together, because a website that brings in calls does little good if the phone is answered poorly or the paperwork is incomplete. You also get ongoing access to our physicians and business staff for advice as the practice grows.

steps.d: We talk with you about your specialty, the procedures you want to grow and the patients you want to reach. You provide your background, service list, logo, photos and any existing materials.

Our designers, programmers, writers and videographers build the website and print pieces, with AI assisting on drafts and our staff and physicians reviewing the medical content. You review the drafts and tell us what to correct.
We publish the website, deliver the print files and forms, and hand your team the front office manual. You set aside time for your staff to study it and name one person to manage website updates.

We stay available to review how the website and inquiries are performing and to advise on next steps. You bring us your questions, new procedures and any changes in the practice so the materials stay current.

tools.d: This is the software behind your website that lets someone edit pages without knowing how to code. We set it up so your staff can change hours, add a provider or publish a blog post on their own.

This is the practice of structuring and writing a website so Google and other search engines understand what you offer and where. We build it into the code, page titles and content from the start instead of adding it afterward.

This is an organized list of the people who gave you their email address through your website. We connect it to your sign-up forms and e-book downloads so you can send news and promotions to people who asked to hear from you.

These are short professionally filmed clips of you, your office and your services placed on key pages. Our staff videographers produce them because visitors who see and hear the physician are more comfortable making a first call.

glossary.d: The moment a website visitor takes the action you want, such as calling the office, filling out a form or requesting an appointment.
Collecting a prospective patient's contact details, usually through a website form, so your office can follow up with them.
A way of building a website so its layout adjusts automatically to fit a phone, tablet or desktop screen.

deliverables.d: A website designed and coded for your practice, not a template, that works on phones and is built so search engines can read it.
Sign-up forms and physician-written e-books that visitors download in exchange for their email address, building a contact list you own.
Forms patients complete on your website before a visit, set up with HIPAA requirements in mind and with your compliance contact.
Our employee manual that teaches your front desk staff how to handle new patient calls, answer questions and book consultations.
Consent forms, physician procedure notes, diagrams and pre and post treatment instructions for the procedures you perform, ready for your own review.
A practice brochure, patient information and referral brochures, a 6×9 services postcard and business cards, all designed to match each other.

fit: you pay for more than one marketing channel and cannot say which one brings in new patients
your front desk is busy with calls but nobody knows what prompted people to pick up the phone
you want to base next year's marketing budget on recorded results instead of impressions and guesses
analytics-call-tracking.plain: Analytics and call tracking is a measurement system that records every call, form, chat and online booking your marketing produces, and shows which campaign each one came from. Without it, a practice sees its marketing bill but cannot tell which part of that spending brought in patients. With it, you can compare channels by what each inquiry cost and decide where to put your budget based on evidence.

steps.d: We talk through every way a patient can reach you today: phone lines, forms, chat and booking software. You tell us which marketing channels you run and who handles compliance at your practice.

We create the tracking numbers, connect your forms and booking tool, and configure privacy settings with HIPAA requirements in mind, together with your compliance contact. You give us access to the website and ad accounts and approve the call recording notice.

We place test calls and submit test forms from each source to confirm everything is counted correctly and still reaches your front desk. You get dashboard access and a short walkthrough for you and your staff.

Each month we send the report, hold the review call and adjust campaigns based on what the data shows. You tell us which inquiries became real appointments, which makes the numbers more useful over time.

tools.d: These are local phone numbers that forward to your regular line and record which ad or listing the caller saw. We assign one to each source through our own phone tracking system, and your existing number stays the same.

This is software that counts visitors to your website and shows which pages they read before contacting you. We set it up so that health information patients share with you is not passed to advertising platforms.
This is a single screen that pulls numbers from your phone tracking, website, booking tool and ad accounts into one place. We build and maintain it, so you do not have to log in to several systems.

This is software that can read a call transcript and write a short summary of it. We use it to draft summaries of recorded calls, which our team reviews; it never speaks with patients or gives medical advice.

glossary.d: The process of working out which ad, search result or listing led a particular patient to contact you.
Any action you want a website visitor to take, such as calling, filling in a form or booking an appointment.
The amount spent on a channel divided by the number of calls, forms and bookings it produced.

deliverables.d: A private web page you can open at any time to see calls, forms, bookings and costs side by side, updated continuously.
A separate phone number for each campaign, all ringing at your front desk, so every call is credited to the right source.
Every contact form, chat conversation and online appointment request is counted and tied to the ad, search or page that led to it.
AI drafts short summaries of recorded calls and our team reviews them, so you learn which treatments and questions patients raise most.
A written report each month that explains what happened, what each channel cost per inquiry, and what we think it means.
A regular conversation where we go through the numbers together and agree on what to change, keep or stop next.

mobile-apps.plain: A mobile app is a program patients install on their phone from the Apple App Store or Google Play, with your practice's name and logo on the icon. It puts booking, reminders, offers and messages one tap away, and it gives you a way to see and run your practice from your own phone. A practice needs one when it wants patients to come back often and wants to reach them without depending on email or social media.

deliverables.d: Two apps, one for each kind of phone, built from a single code base so they look and work the same.
Screens, icon and colors designed to match your website and your office, so patients recognize you at once.
Your app published under your practice's name in the App Store and on Google Play, with screenshots and descriptions written for you.
Messages that appear on the patient's phone for reminders, open slots and offers, sent by you or automatically.
The app talks to your booking system, website and CRM, so appointments and patient details stay in one place.
We keep the app working as Apple and Google release new phone software, and add features as your practice grows.

steps.d: We agree on what the app should do first for your patients and for you. You tell us which systems you use for booking and records.
We design the screens and the icon and show you a version you can tap through on your own phone. You approve it before anything is built.
We build both apps, connect them to your systems and test them on real phones. Your staff tries the app and tells us what to change.
We submit the app to Apple and Google, handle their review and launch it to your patients. After that we watch how it is used and release updates.

tools.d: The only place iPhone owners can install apps. We set up your developer account, prepare the listing and handle Apple's review.
The store for Android phones. We publish and update your app there in step with the iPhone version.
A way of writing one app that runs on both iPhone and Android. We use it so you pay for one build and both apps stay in sync.
Short messages that appear on a phone's lock screen from your app. We set up reminders and offers, and patients choose whether to receive them.

fit: your patients return for repeat treatments and you want to stay in front of them between visits
you want to see your schedule, leads and messages from your phone
you sell products, memberships or packages and want patients to buy and rebook easily

glossary.d: An app installed from a store that lives on the phone, as opposed to a website opened in a browser.
A message your app sends to a patient's phone, which shows up even when the app is closed.
The check Apple and Google run on every app and update before they allow it in their stores.

integrations.plain: An integration is a connection that lets two pieces of software share information automatically. It means the website, app, AI agents and campaigns we build can work with the systems your practice already uses, so you keep your tools and nobody has to copy data by hand. It is possible whenever your current tool offers an API or webhooks, which are the standard ways software lets other software in.

deliverables.d: A check of each tool you use to see whether it offers an API or webhooks and what it allows.
A plain-language map of what information moves between which systems, and when.
The links themselves, built and tested so bookings, leads and messages reach the right system.
Follow-ups, reminders and review requests that start on their own when something happens in one of your tools.
We watch the connections and fix them when a vendor changes something, before it affects your office.
A short written record of what is connected and how, so you are never dependent on memory.

steps.d: You tell us what you use for records, scheduling, phones, payments and marketing. We look up what each one allows.
We show you what can connect, what cannot and what we recommend. You decide what is worth building first.
We build the connections and test them with sample data before any real patient information moves.
After launch we keep watching the connections and adjust them as your tools and your practice change.

tools.d: A doorway a software company provides so other programs can read or send information. We use your vendor's API to exchange bookings, leads and messages.
Automatic notices one system sends to another the moment something happens, such as a new booking. We use them to start follow-ups right away.
Services that link apps without custom code. We use them for simple connections and build custom ones when more control is needed.
Assistants that can use those connections to check open times or log a request. They work only with the access you approve.

fit: you are happy with your EMR or scheduler and do not want to replace it
your staff retypes the same information into more than one system
you want your website, ads and front desk to share one view of each patient

glossary.d: Short for application programming interface: the official way one program lets another exchange information with it.
A message one system sends automatically to another when a specific event happens.
A connection where a change in either system is reflected in the other.
